frontMatter.value: Design deep modules at any step: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface, with the layers a reader must trace and the state a reader must hold kept small. Use when designing or improving one module's interface, placing a seam, making code testable, finding code hard to trace, or exploring alternative interfaces; a repository-wide survey belongs to architecture-survey.

passages.text: deep-modules is the habit for the moment one module's interface is designed or improved, a seam placed, code made testable, or code found hard to trace, at whatever step the work is in, most often build. It writes no record of its own, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run: tdd consults it for the vocabulary of the seam it tests at, and a repository-wide survey is architecture-survey's. passages.text:
### 2. Make the designs, one after another

Make three or more designs in turn: yourself, one after another, or one fresh agent per design through the harness's delegation, each named in the section of the step it serves and counted in no cost, each started only once the one before it has returned its design. Never run them in parallel. Each agent gets the one brief every fresh agent gets, with this page as the skill it works by and its design's technical brief and constraint, below, as its extras; it starts no agent of its own and writes its design as its report, named for the step the design serves, which that step's section cites.
passages.reason: Spawn 3+ sub-agents in parallel becomes three or more designs made in turn, by the one agent or by delegated agents one after another, named in the section they serve and counted in no cost (R21 with R20), each agent briefed and its design named as the ledger guide gives every fresh agent, delegating nothing. Since J-93 S2 the front names greenline's homes and commands by their nouns, their paths and commands on the skill's references page.
passages.gist: Designs made in turn, never in parallel, each agent briefed once

and R21 with R20, the designs made one after another, by the one agent in turn or by delegated agents one after another where the mode spends them, never in parallel; The operator's cards of 2026-10-14 on part 3 of the-whole-change, each "Rule as proposed": one agent at a time through the harness's delegation, in the change's one checkout and never a worktree; one brief for every fresh agent, the change's front matter, its acceptance, its id, the path of its report and the skill it works by, then the step's extras, and no fresh agent delegates; every fresh agent's report is <step>-<n>.md in the change's folder; the fix rounds are per step, and a fix after verify is not reviewed again outside a loop without the owner's word; verify's verdicts stand as the agent gave them; and where the harness has no delegation the block's fallback runs every depth above written; The operator's cards of 2026-10-14 on part 5 of the-whole-change, the walk's cures: "A branch of its own", a change's commits never going to another change's branch, the new change taking greenline/<id> from the default branch where a remote exists and the default branch itself where there is none; "At the proposal", the change's id chosen when the proposal is written, its branch, working folder and record taking the same id; "Yes, every stop commits", every stop committing the record with the change's trailer, so a stopped change is found from any branch and after a clone and resumes on the branch that commit sits on; "Not counted", an agent a step's method starts named in that step's section and counted nowhere; "The one brief, the method's extras", that agent getting the one brief with the extras the page that starts it names; and "Settle in S6" for the orientation's edges and the setup's, the default branch being origin/HEAD, else init.defaultBranch, else the branch HEAD names, and a remote that is no forge offering the local merge or the branch left, never a pull request; The operator's words of 2026-10-18 on the redesign (N-56, items 2 and 7), "we need the upstream prose upfront and references hold how to work meaning the artefacts etc" and, on the ingest procedures, "we wanna have there prose .. what we don't wanna have is there artefact system and fit them to use ours": a skill's front is the upstream prose its recipe cuts, and greenline's mechanics, where the step's work lands, its section's form, its commands and its depths at each mode, stand on its references page (J-93 S2)
